project.name: GraphicsMagick
project.commit_note: The sample metadata leaves `vulnerable_commit` empty. All line anchors below were resolved against the staged vulnerable checkout at `_work/src/graphicsmagick` on commit `e4dd1d93ae60fb0a14f0cf3d7c54e767ba1663fe`, which still lacks the `*q++=image->colormap[index];` write that `patch.diff` adds in the 2-bit `ReadPDBImage()` loop.

analysis_state.reviewer_feedback_resolution: The staged `poc` bytes `ff 20` at offsets `0x4c-0x4d` do not force the second-record block because `PDBInfo.number_records` is declared as signed `short int` in the exact staged source. `ReadBlobMSBShort()` yields `0xff20`, the assignment stores signed value `-224`, `pdb_info.number_records > 1` is therefore false, and the parser reaches image-header bytes `01 00` at offsets `0x76-0x77`, which do select the 2-bit path.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in PDB ReadPDBImage() where DirectClass pixels may use uninitialized memory.
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 146-byte PDB blob in `gt_results/arvo_7350/poc` (sha256 `a7265e2aaa2f46db28c0d36cef4a81c1a63bd1a8d2a3da7ce29fb44754e010bd`). `ReadPDBImage()` admits the `vIMG` / `View` header and reads `number_records` bytes `ff 20` from offsets `0x4c-0x4d`; because `PDBInfo.number_records` is a signed `short int`, that assignment stores `-224`, so the `if (pdb_info.number_records > 1)` block is skipped. The first record header bytes at `0x52-0x55` still pass validation, the optional two-byte skip is false because `offset == 0x20202020`, and the image header therefore begins immediately at `0x56`. There, `pdb_image.version == 0x01` and `pdb_image.type == 0x00`, so the reader chooses the RLE-compressed 2-bit path; `pdb_image.width == 32` and `pdb_image.height == 4`, so `packets == 32`. The remaining two file bytes `ff 20` make `DecodeImage()` expand a run of `0x20` bytes into the full 32-byte raster buffer. In the vulnerable 2-bit loop, `SetImagePixels()` exposes a heap-backed `PixelPacket` row from the pixel cache, but the loop writes only `indexes[x]` and never assigns the matching direct pixel `*q++=image->colormap[index]` that the 1-bit and 4-bit loops perform. `SyncImagePixels()` commits rows whose palette indexes are defined but whose direct pixels remain the uninitialized heap bytes from the cache allocation. When the fuzz target writes the decoded image back out as PDB, `WritePDBImage()` exports each row as 8-bit gray; `ExportGrayQuantumType()` then reads `GetGraySample(p)` from those stale direct pixels, stores the byte in `scanline`, and `WritePDBImage()` packs that byte into its RLE `buffer`. The duplicate-run test at `coders/pdb.c:960` branches on that uninitialized buffer byte, producing the saved MemorySanitizer report. The fix adds the missing `*q++=image->colormap[index];` write in the 2-bit reader loop.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled PDB header state that governs whether the parser skips the second-record block and reaches the vulnerable image decode path.
source.value_from: In the exact staged `poc`, offsets `0x3c-0x43` are ASCII `vIMGView`, and offsets `0x4c-0x4d` are bytes `ff 20`. `ReadBlobMSBShort()` returns unsigned `0xff20`, but `PDBInfo.number_records` is declared as signed `short int`, so this assignment stores signed value `-224` in the staged build.
source.note: This signed record-count value is the decisive source fact for the witness: it later makes `pdb_info.number_records > 1` false, so the parser does not consume the invalid second-record header bytes at `0x56-0x5d` and instead reaches the image header at `0x56`.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `WritePDBImage()` branches on an RLE buffer byte that was packed from a grayscale scanline entry derived from an uninitialized direct pixel.
sink.note: The saved MSan trace reports the primary use at `WritePDBImage /src/graphicsmagick/coders/pdb.c:960:15`, with the immediately preceding tainted store at `pdb.c:955`.

root_cause.description: Patch site. In the 2-bit PDB reader loop, GraphicsMagick stores only the palette index and omits the matching direct-pixel write, leaving the corresponding `PixelPacket` entry uninitialized.
root_cause.note: The 1-bit and 4-bit loops both execute `*q++=image->colormap[index];`. The fix inserts that missing assignment immediately after `indexes[x]=index;` in this 2-bit loop.

tainted_value_origin.description: Heap allocation of the pixel cache backing the row returned by `SetImagePixels()`. MemorySanitizer's origin stack attributes the uninitialized bytes to this allocation.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved origin stack is `malloc -> MagickRealloc -> OpenCache -> ModifyCache -> SetCacheNexus -> SetCacheViewPixels -> ReadPDBImage:574`, showing that the stale direct pixels come from the cache allocation that the 2-bit reader later leaves unwritten.

parser_admitted.description: The exact staged witness passes the `vIMG` / `View` signature check, so execution stays in `ReadPDBImage()` and continues into record-header and image-header parsing.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged PDB header is admitted, signed `number_records == -224` skips the second-record block, and image-header bytes `01 00` select the 2-bit RLE decode path for a 32x4 image.

RLE tail `ff 20` expands to the 32 raster bytes the image needs, `SetImagePixels()` exposes a heap-backed row from the pixel cache, and the vulnerable 2-bit loop fills only `indexes[x]` while leaving direct pixels uninitialized.

When the fuzz target writes the decoded image back out as PDB, the writer exports cached rows as 8-bit gray and reads `GetGraySample(p)` from the stale direct `PixelPacket` entries instead of the defined palette indexes.
The uninitialized grayscale byte is packed into the writer's RLE buffer, and the duplicate-run comparison at line 960 branches on it, matching the saved MSan report.

fine_trace.note: Source. Reads the exact witness's PDB signature and record-count fields. The bytes `ff 20` become signed `-224` when assigned into `short int pdb_info.number_records`.
The first record header bytes at offsets `0x4e-0x55` parse as `offset == 0x20202020`, `tag == "@o\x80"`, and `record_type == 0x01`, so this validation passes and execution stays on the decode path.
Present-but-false offset-adjustment guard. After step 2, `TellBlob(image) == 0x56`, so `0x20202020 - 0x56 != 6`; no extra bytes are skipped and the next unread byte remains at file offset `0x56`.

Signed control decision. Because step 1 stored `pdb_info.number_records == -224`, the predicate `pdb_info.number_records > 1` is false and the parser skips the entire second-record block instead of consuming bytes `0x56-0x5d` as another record header.

With step 4's false branch, the image header starts at offset `0x56`. The exact witness therefore yields `pdb_image.version == 0x01`, `pdb_image.type == 0x00`, `pdb_image.width == 0x0020` (32), and `pdb_image.height == 0x0004` (4).
The parsed header becomes a 32x4 image with `bits_per_pixel == 2`, so the reader expects `packets == 32` compressed raster bytes and will take the vulnerable `case 2` decode arm.
Version `0x01` selects RLE decode. The only remaining file bytes are `ff 20`, so `DecodeImage()` interprets them as one repeat run and fills the 32-byte `pixels` buffer with byte value `0x20`.

The 2-bit loop acquires the current row's direct-pixel buffer `q` and its palette-index buffer `indexes`. The saved MSan origin stack names this site because `SetImagePixels()` exposes heap-backed pixel-cache storage that the caller must initialize.

Root cause. Each decoded `0x20` byte yields in-range 2-bit indexes, so `VerifyColormapIndex` passes and the loop stores `indexes[x]`. But this arm never performs the matching `*q++=image->colormap[index];` write, so the corresponding direct pixel `q[x]` remains the uninitialized cache byte from step 8.

The row is committed with defined palette indexes but still-uninitialized direct pixels. `SyncImagePixels()` syncs the cache view; it does not synthesize `PixelPacket` values from the indexes written in step 9.

Later, the fuzzer's writeback path reacquires that cached row and asks GraphicsMagick to export it as an 8-bit grayscale scanline. This dispatches into `ExportViewPixelArea()` and then `ExportGrayQuantumType()`.

The gray exporter ignores palette indexes and reads `GetGraySample(p)` from the direct `PixelPacket` row, then stores that byte into `scanline`. Because step 9 never initialized `q[x]`, this is the use-before-init read named by the saved intermediate MSan stack.
The writer packs the tainted grayscale byte from `scanline[x]` into its RLE output buffer. This matches the saved MSan intermediate store at `pdb.c:955`.
Sink. The writer's duplicate-run comparison branches on the uninitialized buffer byte from step 13, which is the saved MemorySanitizer use site.

allocation_context.note: The saved origin stack names heap allocation in `OpenCache`; the exact staged source line performing it is `MagickReallocMemory(PixelPacket *,cache_info->pixels,(size_t) offset);` at line 3177.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The saved allocation context is the heap pixel-cache storage created in `OpenCache` and exposed through `SetImagePixels()` at `ReadPDBImage:574`; step 9 is the exact place where the 2-bit loop leaves one of those `PixelPacket` entries unwritten.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The byte-level source path closes `ReadPDBImage` through steps 1-10, the saved intermediate MSan store stack matches steps 12-13 (`ExportGrayQuantumType:733` then `WritePDBImage:955`), and the primary crash stack matches sink step 14 at `WritePDBImage:960`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact staged bytes source-groundedly select the 2-bit reader path, RLE-decode to byte `0x20`, populate only `indexes[]` in the vulnerable loop, and later cause `ExportGrayQuantumType()` to read the stale direct pixel that `WritePDBImage()` packs and branches on at the sink.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the missing `*q++=image->colormap[index];` assignment immediately after `indexes[x]=index;` in the 2-bit reader loop, which makes the direct-pixel row defined before the later export and writeback.

poc.trigger: Feed the exact staged 146-byte witness in `gt_results/arvo_7350/poc` (sha256 `a7265e2aaa2f46db28c0d36cef4a81c1a63bd1a8d2a3da7ce29fb44754e010bd`) into `coder_PDB_fuzzer`. The blob passes the `vIMG` / `View` header check, stores `number_records` bytes `ff20` that become signed `-224`, so the second-record block is skipped; image-header bytes `01 00` at offsets `0x76-0x77` then select the RLE-compressed 2-bit path for a 32x4 image. The trailing bytes `ff 20` RLE-expand to the 32 raster bytes the image needs, the 2-bit loop writes only `indexes[]` and not direct pixels, and the later writeback reproduces the saved MemorySanitizer branch on `WritePDBImage:960`.

format.name: exact staged 146-byte PDB / FireViewer witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 146-byte blob in `poc`, whose visible fixed fields are: `vIMGView` at offsets `0x3c-0x43`, signed record-count bytes `ff20` at `0x4c-0x4d`, first-record bytes `40 6f 80 01` at `0x52-0x55`, image-header version/type bytes `01 00` at `0x76-0x77`, width/height bytes `00 20 00 04` at `0x8c-0x8f`, and compressed tail `ff 20` at `0x90-0x91`. On the exact staged source this means `pdb_info.number_records == -224`, `bits_per_pixel == 2`, `image->columns == 32`, `image->rows == 4`, and `DecodeImage()` fills the 32-byte raster buffer with `0x20`. This GT is grounded only for that exact witness layout; it does not generalize to arbitrary negative `number_records` values or other PDB record/header encodings.
